questions.question: Arrange the oxoacids of chlorine HClO, HClO₂, HClO₃ and HClO₄ in order of increasing acid strength and explain the trend. ($K_a$: 3.0 × 10⁻⁸, 4.0 × 10⁻², 5 × 10¹, 10¹⁰)
questions.solution:
**Order of increasing acid strength:**

$$\text{HClO} < \text{HClO}_2 < \text{HClO}_3 < \text{HClO}_4$$

This matches the increase in $K_a$ from $3.0 \times 10^{-8}$ to $10^{10}$.

**Explanation.**

Each extra oxygen atom pulls electrons away from the O–H bond through its strong $-I$ inductive effect, so the O–H bond becomes weaker and the proton is lost more easily. The $O^-$ groups generated are also stabilised by resonance delocalisation over several oxygens, making the conjugate base more stable and the acid stronger.

Pauling's empirical rule, $pK_a \approx 8 - 5m$ where $m$ is the number of non-protonated oxygen atoms, confirms it: HClO ($m=0$) gives $pK_a \approx 8$; HClO₂ ($m=1$) $pK_a \approx 3$; HClO₃ ($m=2$) $pK_a \approx -2$; HClO₄ ($m=3$) $pK_a \approx -7$. Perchloric acid is thus one of the strongest acids known.
questions.knowledgeNote: Acid strength of oxoacids rises with each added oxygen because of the inductive effect and resonance stabilisation of the anion.
